Ukraine grapples with a shortage of troops at the front after over 4 years of war
A shortage of combat-ready troops has plagued Ukraine ever since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022
KYIV, Ukraine -- Ukraine’s advances in drone technology and tactics have captured the world’s attention. Despite those innovations, one problem has plagued the country since the start of Russia’s invasion: a shortage of combat-ready troops.
Ukraine always has been outmanned by Russia, but as the war drags through its fifth year, the need for personnel is increasingly acute, commanders and analysts say, with some units at only half strength. There just aren't enough forces to fully exploit the battlefield advantages resulting from the drone innovations.
“Based on the equipment and the number of people we have today, we barely have enough to hold the sector we currently have,” said a deputy commander of the Da Vinci Wolves battalion in eastern Ukraine's Pokrovsk area, a focus of Russia’s offensive.
“To move forward would inevitably mean greater losses,” said the deputy commander, who insisted on identifying himself only as “Afer” because of military rules.
Long-standing mobilization problems, including draft dodging and desertion, make it harder for Ukraine to build its reserves, according to military experts, resulting in only incremental changes along the 1,250-kilometer (775-mile) front line.
Ukraine needs to be able to commit forces quickly without taking them from elsewhere on the front. Otherwise, commanders have fewer options to turn a temporary advantage into a sustained operation, said Nick Reynolds of the U.K.-based Royal United Services Institute, a defense and security think tank.
The shortage means that units can't be rotated often enough, he said, “leading to exhaustion and, in turn, exacerbating casualties.”
The Defense Ministry, which in July underwent a shake-up by President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, is trying to tackle the problem with reforms to mobilization, training and the way the army is organized.
Uneven performance by front-line units worsens the problem. Weaker formations suffer heavier losses, creating a cycle of high attrition and constant replenishment.
The ministry did not respond to Associated Press requests for comment, but one of its officials summarized the problem by saying, “There just are not enough people.”
Developing a new mobilization policy, including encouraging deserters to return to duty, is among the most sensitive issues under consideration, said the official, who was not authorized to brief the media and spoke on condition of anonymity.
Former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, who was replaced by Yevhenii Khmara in the summer shake-up by Zelenskyy, had sought to reorganize the military around fewer but stronger units. He wanted to reinforce those that performed well and disband the weaker ones.
Khmara has said he wants to continue those changes.
But the reforms will take time. Yehor Cherniev, a member of parliament's defense committee, said lawmakers have yet to see mobilization initiatives.
In June, Fedorov introduced reforms to military contracts designed to make infantry service more attractive by offering higher salaries and fixed terms of service.
Convincing Ukrainians who have little incentive to fight is a major challenge after more than four years of war, and the country is struggling to recruit enough troops from its estimated population of 39 million.
The pool of men aged 25-60 is relatively small following years of demographic decline from war-related displacement and migration. There are about 6.8 million men aged 25-59, according to U.N. figures provided by Ukraine's National Health System, but that includes wounded veterans and men otherwise unable to serve.
Official figures put the military’s strength at about 1 million, with only a small fraction deployed at the front.
Compulsory service applies only to men. Women are allowed to volunteer, and those with medical or pharmaceutical training are required to register with the military. Over 70,000 women are serving in the army, according to Defense Ministry statistics in January 2025.
In March, Fedorov said about 2 million Ukrainian men were evading service, while about 200,000 soldiers had deserted or left their units without authorization. The penalty for desertion is imprisonment of up to 12 years.
Some men flee the country illegally or hide at home. Recruiters sometimes stop them on streets and trains, and those without valid exemptions are sent into the army. In January 2025, the government said about 950,000 men had deferments at the request of businesses.
Russia, with an estimated population of 143 million, also is struggling to fill its military ranks. It launched a widely unpopular partial mobilization of 300,000 reservists months after launching the invasion, and hundreds of thousands of men fled abroad. Since then, the Kremlin has relied on volunteers lured by relatively high pay and benefits to sustain its force of what President Vladimir Putin has said numbers about 700,000 men fighting in Ukraine.
Ukraine's problem is not so much a shortage of personnel but how they are managed and deployed, said military analyst Taras Chmut, who also heads Come Back Alive, a charity providing assistance to the army.
Increasing the number of personnel in the defense forces does not necessarily increase their effectiveness, Chmut said.
Exhaustion, poor organization, inadequate training and the lack of a clear end-of-service date drive recruits to desert, according to soldiers and military analysts.
The consequences are felt immediately at the front, with fewer troops to replace battered units or available for emergencies, and a diminished ability to divert forces when an opening appears. Drones can sometimes alleviate the shortages.
With replacements scarce, some troops have spent up to a year at the front with little opportunity for rotation, said Afer, the deputy commander of the Da Vinci Wolves battalion. His unit is operating at only about half its strength while its area of responsibility has doubled, he said, meaning the same number of forces must defend about twice the territory.
Ideally, at least twice as many men are needed simply to hold current positions, but that doesn't take into account that a constant reserve of troops is needed to replace casualties, he said.
It's also a struggle to find qualified specialists who can operate increasingly sophisticated equipment on the battlefield, Afer said, adding that troops “who know how to think” are in short supply.
Ukraine can conduct localized offensives but not enough to shift the broader battlefield balance, despite mounting Russian losses. Even so, it has retaken territory in several areas, including in operations near the eastern city of Lyman.
Pavlo Narozhnyi, a Ukrainian military analyst, said he did not consider manpower an insurmountable problem for simply holding the defensive line.
“We can do limited offensives,” he said, pointing to recent actions in the Dnipropetrovsk and Lyman areas, “but it’s relatively small.”
Russian forces have occupied roughly 990 square kilometers (about 380 square miles) of Ukrainian territory since the beginning of 2026, while Ukrainian forces have retaken about 820 square kilometers (316 square miles), according to figures cited by Zelenskyy, who added that Kyiv aims to bring those figures closer to parity by year's end.
But RUSI's Reynolds said there would not be fundamental changes to the broader battlefield balance, with the front line essentially remaining the same.
——
Associated Press reporter Volodymyr Yurchuk contributed.

Quick Answer
macOS 27 Golden Gate has far more useful features than the ones you will notice immediately after updating. I tested more than 27 of them and picked the 27 worth trying, including Siri AI, custom Safari extensions, smarter Shortcuts, new Photos tools, and several smaller additions. Go through this list, and you will likely find a few features that can make the way you use your Mac easier.
Apple has finally released macOS 27 Golden Gate, and unlike the last few macOS updates, this one feels like a much bigger update. Apple has changed how macOS looks, added the new Siri AI, brought several Apple Intelligence features to its built-in apps, and made noticeable changes to Safari, Photos, Notes, Calendar, and many other places that you will notice once you start using your Mac.
I have been using macOS 27 and trying these features on my Mac, and some of them are genuinely useful. Some of my favorites is the new Siri that does many more things than previous, also Safari that lets you create your own extension simply by describing what you want it to do.
There are plenty of smaller additions like this throughout macOS 27. Some solve problems I have had with macOS for a long time, while others add things that previously required a third-party app or a much longer workaround. In this article, I will show you the best macOS 27 Golden Gate features I have found so far, what has changed, and how you can try them on your Mac.
Table of Contents
27 Best macOS 27 Golden Gate Features
macOS 27 Golden Gate comes with countless new features and small changes, and covering every single one of them in one article isn’t possible. After digging deeper into the update and trying many of these features myself, I have picked the best 27 that I found the most useful and that I think most Mac users should know about. Some are easy to notice, while others are hidden inside the apps and settings you already use every day.
Talk With Siri AI and Continue Your Previous Conversations
Siri has received one of its biggest changes on the Mac with macOS 27. Instead of only appearing as the small Siri interface we have been using for years, Siri AI now has its own app where you can start a conversation, ask follow-up questions, and return to your previous conversations later.
This is particularly useful when I have already given Siri all the context about something, and whenever needed, I can reopen that conversation instead of explaining everything again.
To use the Siri AI app on your Mac, first make sure Siri is enabled.
Once it is enabled, open the Siri app, where you will find all your previous conversations in the left sidebar and the chat window on the right. You can select any previous conversation to continue chatting or start a new conversation with Siri. If you right-click on any conversation in the sidebar, you will also see additional options to pin or delete the conversation.
Search Your Mac and Ask Siri Directly From Spotlight
Spotlight is one of the features I use almost every day on my Mac. With macOS 27, it also becomes a quick way to access Siri AI, so I don’t have to open the dedicated Siri app whenever I have a small question.
You just have to press Command + Space to open Spotlight and continue typing normally when you want to find an app, file, document, or setting. When you want to ask Siri AI something instead, just type your query normally and hit return to get an answer. You can also access whatever you have searched in Spotlight in the dedicated Siri app as a separate conversation.
I prefer using this for quick questions and keeping the Siri app for longer conversations where I know I will need follow-up questions.
Create Your Own Safari Extension Just by Describing It
Safari already supports extensions, but I still have to find an extension that does exactly what I need. With macOS 27, I can simply describe the functionality I want, and Safari can create an extension for me using Apple Intelligence.
I tried this with Instagram. I sometimes watch Reels on Instagram’s website, but it doesn’t give me a playback bar to quickly move forward or backward in a Reel. Instead of searching for an extension, I asked Safari to create one using this prompt:
Prompt: Create an extension for Instagram that adds playback controls to Reels and lets me move forward or backwards in the video while watching a Reel.
Surprisingly, it worked. After enabling the generated extension, I could seek forward and backwards while watching Instagram Reels. If there is a small website-specific feature you have always wanted, this gives you a way to try building it yourself.
To create one:
- Open Safari on your Mac and visit the website for which you want to create an extension.
- Click on the Page menu inside Safari’s address bar and select Describe Extension.
- Describe exactly what you want the extension to do. “I recommend keeping the request focused on one particular problem instead of asking it to change several unrelated things on the website.”
- Safari will first check whether an existing extension from the App Store can do what you described. If you don’t want one of the suggested extensions, click Create to generate your own.
- Once Safari creates the extension, click Try and test it on the website. Don’t save it immediately; use the website normally for a few minutes and make sure the extension actually behaves the way you expected.
- If something isn’t working correctly, click Edit and describe what you want Safari to change. Once you are happy with the result, click Save to keep the extension.
If you are new to browser extensions, you can check our list of the best Safari extensions for Mac to see what else extensions can add to Safari.
Create Shortcuts by Simply Explaining What You Want
Shortcuts can automate plenty of repetitive tasks on a Mac, but creating a complicated shortcut manually isn’t always easy. macOS 27 lets you describe what you want in normal language, and Apple Intelligence can put together the required Shortcut actions for you.
For example, I created a simple shortcut for work. Whenever I start working, I need to open TechPP, Gmail, Google Docs, and WordPress. Instead of opening each website manually, I created a shortcut that opens all four websites in Chrome whenever I run it.
Prompt: Create a shortcut that opens techpp.com, Gmail, Google Docs, and WordPress in Chrome.
Here’s how you can create it:
- Open the Shortcuts app on your Mac and click the plus (+) button.
- Enter the prompt in the Describe a shortcut field and let Apple Intelligence create the shortcut for you.
- Once it is created, click Run or the Play icon to test it.
Use Visual Intelligence to Understand What’s on Your Screen
Visual Intelligence on the Mac works differently from the camera-based experience on the iPhone. In macOS 27, I can select something already visible on my screen and ask Siri AI about it, which is useful when the thing I am looking at is easier to show than describe.
Suppose I see a chair in an image and want to know what kind of chair it is or find similar designs. Instead of describing its shape, material, and appearance, I can press Command + Shift + 6, select the chair on the screen, and choose Ask Siri to ask about it. There is also an Image Search option when I want to find visually similar results online.
Adjust How Much Liquid Glass You Want on Your Mac
Apple introduced Liquid Glass across its operating systems last year, but macOS 27 now gives you more control over how transparent the interface actually looks. Instead of having to accept one fixed appearance, there is now a slider that lets you choose how clear or tinted you want Liquid Glass to be.
To adjust it:
- Open the System Settings on your Mac and click Appearance in the sidebar.
- Find the Liquid Glass adjustment inside the Appearance settings.
- Move the slider toward the left if you want the interface to look clearer and more transparent. Move it toward the right if you want more tint and less of the background showing through.
Hide Extra Menu Bar Icons and Access Them When You Need Them
My Mac’s menu bar gets crowded quickly because several utilities I use throughout the day add their own icons. macOS 27 handles this better with a new overflow control that hides icons when there isn’t enough space and gives you a double-arrow button to reveal them whenever you need them. This means I don’t have to remove a useful menu bar utility just because I don’t need its icon visible every minute. This is especially useful on MacBooks with a notch, where menu bar space is already limited.
Let Safari Automatically Organise Your Tabs Into Topics
I am terrible at keeping my browser tabs under control, particularly when I am researching something and have several unrelated pages open at the same time. Safari already has Tab Groups on Mac, which are useful when you manually organize related tabs. macOS 27 takes this a step further by using Apple Intelligence to automatically identify related tabs and organize them into topics. Each topic gets a label and a tab count, and you can collapse a topic when you aren’t working on it without actually closing those tabs.
For example, while researching for this article, I might have 10–15 tabs open about different macOS features, along with a few Amazon shopping tabs and some work-related pages. Instead of showing all of them together in one long row, Safari can automatically identify which tabs are related and organise them into separate topics such as macOS 27, Shopping, and Work. I can keep the macOS 27 topic expanded while I am researching and collapse Shopping and Work to hide those tabs temporarily. Whenever I need them again, I can simply expand that topic without having to search through all my open tabs.
To enable it:
- Open Safari on your Mac and click Safari in the menu bar at the top left of the screen.
- Choose Settings, and then switch to Tabs section.
- Then click the drop-down menu right to Organise tabs and select Automatically Create Topics.
- Continue browsing normally and open a few pages related to the same subject. Safari will identify related tabs and place them under a topic when it recognises the connection.
Change the Perspective of a Photo With Reframe
Cropping can remove unnecessary space from a photo, but it can’t change the angle from which the photo appears to have been taken. The new Reframe feature goes further by using Apple Intelligence to change the perspective and angle of an existing image.
I find this useful when I like a photo but wish I had taken it from a slightly different angle or positioned the subject differently. To use it:
- Open the Photos app on your Mac and double-click the photo.
- Click the Edit button in the top-right corner to open the photo editing tools.
- Click Tools and select Reframe from the available options.
- Drag the photo or use the available perspective controls to change how you want the final image to be framed. I recommend making smaller adjustments first instead of immediately trying to create a completely different camera angle.
- Once you have the angle you want, click Reframe and wait for Apple Intelligence to generate the additional parts required for the new perspective.
- Pay particular attention to faces, hands, and other objects whose shape is easy to recognize. If everything looks right, Finally click Save Changes.
Expand a Photo Beyond Its Original Frame With Extend
There have been times when I had a good portrait photo but couldn’t use it as a wallpaper or inside a presentation because converting it to a wider aspect ratio would crop an important part of the image, and where the new Extend feature comes in. It generate additional content outside the original frame with Apple Intelligence.
To try it, open the image in Photos, click Edit, and open Tools. Select Extend, drag the edges beyond the original photo or choose the aspect ratio you need, and click Extend to generate the missing area.
Check the newly generated areas carefully before saving the result. If you don’t like what it created, adjust the frame and try again instead of keeping an obviously generated section.
Remove Unwanted Objects From Photos With Clean Up
Apple introduced the Clean Up tool with Apple Intelligence, and macOS 27 improves how it handles larger unwanted objects. If I take a photo at a tourist spot and someone is standing in the background I can select that person and let Photos remove them.
Here’s how you can remove an unwanted object from a photo:
- Open the Photos app on your Mac and double-click the photo you want to edit.
- Click Edit in the upper-right corner and open Tools.
- Select Clean Up, and your Mac will analyse the image. In some cases, Photos may automatically highlight objects it thinks you might want to remove.
- Click on a highlighted object to remove it, or use the Erase brush to paint over the object yourself. You can also circle the object if that makes it easier to select.
- And, finally, click Clean Up.
Resize the iPhone Mirroring Window
iPhone Mirroring is useful when I want to access something on my iPhone without picking it up, but using everything inside a phone-sized window on a large Mac display isn’t always ideal. macOS 27 fixes this by letting you resize the iPhone Mirroring window just by dragging its corner. You can also use keyboard shortcuts to quickly resize the iPhone Mirroring window. Press Command + Plus (+) to increase the window size and Command + Minus (-) to decrease it. If you want to return the window to its default size, press Command + 0.
But macOS 27 takes resizing a step further with supported apps. When you open a resizable app and make the iPhone Mirroring window wider, the app can actually adjust its layout and show more content instead of simply making the same iPhone interface bigger.
For example, if I open a supported app and drag the iPhone Mirroring window into a wider layout, I can get more usable screen space and information inside the app. Not every app supports this yet, so in unsupported apps, resizing may simply make the existing interface larger or smaller. You can press Command + 9 whenever you want to return the window to the standard iPhone size.
Let Your Mac Suggest Better Names for Files and Folders
My Downloads folder has taught me how quickly bad filenames can become a problem. A name such as “Untitled” or “Document 2” becomes useless once I forget what is inside them.
With macOS 27, Apple Intelligence can suggest names for files and folders based on what they contain. Instead of having to open a document again just to remember what it was about, macOS can look at the content and suggest a name that actually describes it.
First, you have to make sure this feature is enabled on your Mac. To do so, open Finder and click the Finder button in the menu bar. Next, choose Settings and make sure you are in the General tab. Now, check the box next to Suggest Filenames.
Now, to use this feature, right-click any document, photo, screenshot, or folder in Finder and select Rename. Wait for around five seconds, and Finder will show you a few suggested names based on the file’s contents. You can select the name you like and use it instead of typing one manually.
Create and Edit Calendar Events by Describing Them
macOS 27 makes creating Calendar events faster by describing the event naturally instead of filling in every field separately. I can type something like “Pankaj’s birthday next Monday,” and Calendar can use those details to create the event.
To try it, open Calendar, click the plus (+) button, and enter your description in Describe Event. You can also describe changes to an existing event instead of manually changing individual details.
Draw Directly Inside Apple Notes on Your Mac
Not everything you want to save in a note needs to be written as text. For example, if you’re planning the layout of a room, sketching a quick idea, making a simple diagram, or noting down something that is easier to remember visually, a quick drawing can be more useful than typing it out. With macOS 27, you can now create these drawings directly inside a note on your Mac and keep them saved along with the rest of your notes.
Previously, you could create drawings in a note from an iPhone or iPad, but macOS didn’t let you draw directly inside Notes on the Mac. Now, you can use your mouse or trackpad to create a quick sketch without leaving the Notes app.
Here’s how you can draw inside a note:
- Open the Notes app.
- Click the Markup button in the Notes toolbar to open the drawing tools.
- Choose the drawing tool you want to use, and adjust its thickness and colour depending on what you are trying to draw.
- Start drawing directly inside the note using your mouse or trackpad.
- Once you are finished, click the Markup button again to exit the drawing tools and continue working on the rest of your note.
Generate Images in More Styles With Image Playground
I tested Image Playground on Mac when Apple first introduced it, and one of my biggest complaints was how limited the available styles felt. Now, Apple has made Image Playground much more flexible in macOS 27. You now get more styles, including create photorealistic images, and the Any Style option lets you describe the kind of visual appearance you want instead of choosing only from a small set of presets. You can also choose square, portrait, or landscape output depending on where you plan to use the image.
Another change I find more useful is targeted editing. If most of the generated image looks good but there is one part I want to change, I can select that area and describe the change instead of generating the entire image again and hoping everything else remains the same.
If you are using Image Playground for the first time, I recommend reading our complete Image Playground guide for Mac, where we have covered the interface, creating images, using your own photos, and managing generated images in more detail.
Record Your Mac Screen With System Audio
This is one of my favorite smaller additions in macOS 27, especially because I regularly work on tutorials. macOS has had a built-in screen recorder for a long time, but recording the sound coming directly from the Mac hasn’t been nearly as straightforward as recording the screen itself.
The difference between system audio and microphone audio is important here. If I am recording a tutorial and an app plays a sound, system audio captures that sound directly. I don’t have to turn up my MacBook speakers and let the microphone record them along with keyboard sounds, fan noise, and everything else happening in the room.
Here’s how you can record your Mac screen with system audio:
- Press Shift + Command + 5 on your keyboard to open the built-in screenshot and screen-recording toolbar.
- Choose whether you want to Record Entire Screen, Record Selected Portion, or Selected Window depending on what you want to capture.
- Click Options in the toolbar and enable Include System Audio so that sounds playing on your Mac are included in the recording.
Add Extra-Large Widgets to Your Mac Desktop
I have been using widgets on my Mac desktop since Apple introduced them with macOS Sonoma. but the existing widget sizes don’t always work when an app has more information to show.
macOS 27 adds new Extra Large widget sizes, including a portrait layout for supported widgets. The additional space lets apps show considerably more information on the desktop.
To add an extra large widget on your desktop:
- Right-click anywhere on your Mac desktop and select Edit Widgets.
- Find the app whose widget you want to add and look through the available widget sizes. If the app supports the new sizes, you should see Extra Large or Extra Large Portrait among the options.
- Select the size you want and add the widget to your desktop.
If you haven’t used desktop widgets before, we have a complete guide explaining how to add widgets to your Mac desktop, including how to customise the widgets already on your Mac.
Share Photos and Videos in Full Resolution With Shared Albums
Shared Albums are convenient when I want to collect photos from a trip, event, or family function in one place, but there has always been a compromise: the photos and videos shared through them weren’t necessarily kept in their original quality.
Apple changes that with the new Shared Albums experience in macOS 27. Newly created permanent Shared Albums can store photos and videos at full resolution
Let Android and Windows Users Add Photos to Your Shared Albums
The Shared Albums update gets even more useful if your friends or family don’t all use Apple devices. Previously, you needed several WhatsApp chats, Google Drive folders, and people sending pictures individually
With macOS 27, people on Android and Windows can access the updated Shared Albums through a web browser, and they don’t necessarily need an Apple Account to participate. More importantly, you can allow them to contribute photos instead of limiting them to viewing the album.
Save Any Frame From a Video Directly as a Photo
Sometimes the best photo from a moment is actually hidden inside a video. Before macOS 27, if we spotted an interesting moment in a video, the easiest way to save it as a photo was to take a screenshot. But a screenshot doesn’t preserve the video frame as cleanly as a dedicated photo, and you may end up with lower quality or unwanted elements from the screen. With macOS 27, you can now save any video frame directly as a separate photo in your Photos library.
Open the video in Photos, pause it at the moment you want, and check the nearby frames until you find the best one. Then right-click the frame and select Save Video Frame as Photo. The saved frame appears in your Photos library, where you can edit and share it just like any other photo.
Start a Slideshow Directly From a Photo Album
I usually organise photos from a trip or event into an album, but when I want to show those pictures to someone, opening them one by one isn’t the nicest way to do it. macOS 27 makes this easier by letting me start a slideshow directly from an album in Photos, so I can show the entire collection without having to open every photo individually.
Slideshows themselves aren’t new on the Mac, but I like that I can now start one directly from an album I have already organised. Once the slideshow starts, I can quickly customise how it plays by changing the transition and duration, adding music, and deciding whether it should loop.
Here’s how you can start a slideshow from an album:
- Open the Photos app on your Mac and find the album you want to show.
- Control-click the album and select Start Slideshow from the menu.
- Once the slideshow starts, click Customise if you want to change how it plays.
- Adjust the Transition & Duration settings to control how quickly the photos move from one to another, and choose music if you want something playing in the background.
Change How Fast and Expressive Siri Sounds
I don’t always want Siri to speak at the same pace. If I am following instructions, a slightly slower response can be easier to understand. And if the current voice feels too slow, you can make it speak faster. macOS 27 also lets you change more than just how fast Siri speaks. On supported Macs and voices, you can also adjust how expressive the voice sounds. Increasing this setting gives Siri’s speech more variation and emphasis, which can make the spoken responses feel more natural and animated.
Get Better Resolution Support for External Displays
macOS 27 improves external display support, including 5K at 120Hz on certain compatible ultrawide monitors. Apple has also improved how macOS restores window positions and display arrangements after disconnecting and reconnecting a monitor, which I find more useful when regularly docking and undocking a MacBook.
After connecting your monitor, open System Settings, select Displays, and choose the external monitor to see the available resolutions and refresh rates.
Make Buttons and Other Controls Easier to See With Show Borders
macOS 27 adds a new Show Borders accessibility option that makes the boundaries around buttons and other interface controls easier to distinguish. This can be useful if you don’t want some controls to blend into the background with the Liquid Glass design.
To enable it, open System Settings and click Accessibility in the left sidebar. Select Display from the right-side panel, find Show Borders, and turn on the toggle next to it. You can also try Reduce Transparency from the same section if transparency itself is making parts of the interface difficult to see.
Explore Cities With More Detailed 3D Views in Apple Maps
Apple has improved the 3D city experience in Maps with more detailed buildings and surroundings in supported locations. I don’t use 3D Maps every time I need directions, but it can be useful when I want to understand the layout of an unfamiliar area before visiting it.
To try it, open Maps and search for the city or location you want to explore. Click View in the menu bar, select Show 3D Map, and enable Satellite if you want to explore the area using the detailed imagery.
Try the New Golden Gate Wallpapers and Screen Savers
Finally, macOS 27 comes with new Sunset and Night views of the Golden Gate Bridge, along with a new abstract wallpaper. The Golden Gate scenes can also be used as screen savers.
To try them, open System Settings and select Wallpaper from the left sidebar. Browse through the new macOS 27 backgrounds and select the one you want to use.
macOS 27 Feels More Useful Once You Start Finding the Smaller Changes
After trying more than 27 new macOS 27 features, creating custom Safari extensions is still the one I enjoyed the most, while several smaller additions have also made my everyday Mac experience better. If you enjoyed this guide, also check out our 27 best iOS 27 features you should try on your iPhone.
FAQs about macOS 27
1. Do All macOS 27 Features Work on Every Mac That Supports macOS 27?
No. Your Mac may support macOS 27 but still miss some features because individual features can have additional hardware, language, or region requirements.
2. Can Safari Extensions I Create Be Shared With Other People?
Not directly. Safari’s Describe Extension feature creates custom extensions for your own use. You can sync compatible extensions across your own Apple devices, but Apple currently doesn’t provide an option to send a generated extension directly to another person.
3. Can I Downgrade to macOS 26 After Installing macOS 27?
Yes, as long as macOS 26 supports your Mac. However, downgrading isn’t available like a normal software update and may require erasing your Mac and reinstalling the older macOS version. So, make sure you have a complete backup before proceeding.

The Delhi Police has stepped up its social media campaign ahead of the October 10 protest at Jantar Mantar, with its perception management wing working to counter what officials describe as a “cyber warfare” campaign that, according to the force, had projected the police in a negative light during the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) July demonstration.
“Concentrated efforts are being made to show the police’s side of the story. The effort is being made based on the learning from our past experience during the July protest of the CJP, and efforts are being made to draw engagement on social media platforms,” an official close to the matter said.
The police began examining the performance of their social media content and why their version of events did not receive similar traction during the July protest. Another official close to the development said the force was working with Meta, X and other social media platforms to examine why its content was not being amplified by their algorithms.
A series of videos showing personnel allegedly injured during protests, uniforms and badges that were torn, women officers being assisted after collapsing and instances of protesters allegedly pushing or resisting police personnel have been circulated via the official Delhi police handle on X. Videos also include statements and assessments by senior police officials on incidents during the demonstrations.
According to police officials, the July protest generated a large volume of social media content in support of the demonstrators, while comparatively fewer videos presenting the police’s account of events were circulated. The police believe the imbalance in online content helped shape public perception of the protest and put the force on the defensive.
The Delhi police have identified at least 500 individuals who they believe are likely to attend the protest. The list includes members of the CJP’s core team, supporters and people associated with the organisers, including domestic workers, drivers and other staff, according to the document seen by The Hindu.
Editorial | Saving faces: On protests, biometric surveillance
The police have also identified around 200 WhatsApp and Telegram channels that are being used to “mobilise people for the protest”.
Separately, the force is monitoring at least 100 individuals who describe themselves as “independent journalists”, along with around 20 channels associated with them, officials said. The police said the exercise was aimed at tracking online activity surrounding the protest.
The police’s intensified online outreach marks a shift from its approach during the July protest, when, officials said, the force was largely reacting to a narrative that had already gained traction online.
The force has since sought to increase the volume and reach its own content. Officials said its current strategy includes monitoring material being posted by protesters and others online and then putting out the police’s account of the same incidents.
“We are not posting CCTV footage or any evidence material, but whatever other people are sharing, we are telling our side of the story,” the official said.
The development comes as the Delhi Police prepares for the October 10 protest and steps up surveillance of the online networks being used for mobilisation. The Delhi Police Perception Management and Media Cell division was initiated in October 2021.
At a glance
500 — People identified by the Delhi Police as likely to join the October 10 CJP protest
200 — WhatsApp and Telegram channels identified as being used to mobilise people for the protest
100 — Individuals identifying themselves as “independent journalists” being monitored by the police
20 — Channels associated with such “independent journalists” being tracked by the police

SP chief Akhilesh Yadav has said UP CM Yogi Adityanath should contest from Ayodhya.
NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Thursday challenged Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath to contest the upcoming assembly elections from Ayodhya. Akhilesh also said he would soon visit the Ram temple in Ayodhya along with SP leaders for darshan.Addressing a gathering at a Shrimad Bhagwat Katha organised by SP leader and former Ayodhya MLA Tej Narayan Pandey, also known as Pawan Pandey, Akhilesh claimed the BJP had conducted several surveys since the SP announced its candidate for the Ayodhya seat, reported news agency PTI.
"Ever since we announced our candidate, the BJP has been conducting survey after survey, and it is falling behind in every survey. We are hearing that they have not been able to find a new candidate for Ayodhya," Akhilesh said."If the chief minister, who makes tall claims, is so confident, he should contest the election from Ayodhya himself and prove it," he said.Later, responding to questions from reporters about visiting the Ram temple, Akhilesh said he had earlier decided to do so after the completion of the Kedareshwar Dham temple in Etawah."I had earlier resolved that after the completion of the Kedareshwar Dham, I would ask my party colleague Pawan Pandey to fix a date and we would all visit the Ram temple for darshan," he said.The clarification comes amid BJP's constant attack over his no visit to the Ram temple. The BJP has claimed that despite invitations, he has not offered prayers there owing to Muslim appeasement.

Good Morning Shoppers, It's Caffeine Time

That’s a Wrap on Day One's Deals

Everyone Needs to Hear About This Dish Soap I Bought

Apparently spray-on dish detergent has been around since 2020, but I just became aware of Dawn Powerwash this summer when I saw it on an endcap at the grocery store and bought it on a whim (typically I do grocery pickup to curb my impulse shopping, but this time it paid off!). I am not ashamed to admit that dish spray in a bottle has changed my life. It’s not only a no-mess, only-spray-what-you-need solution for dishes, but you can use it to clean all sorts of things, from clothes to your car. One bottle of Powerwash is $5 at most grocery stores, so not only are you saving $2 a bottle with this deal, it’s being delivered right to your house, so you won’t go to the store and impulse-buy other things. Win-win!
My Best Hair Ever Is Thanks To This Hat
It might look like a baseball cap, but this red light hat unlocked my best hair ever. I'm pregnant now and everyone has compliments for my hair, but I know the real source of this was my red light hat I religiously wore at the end of last year into this year. The HigherDose Red Light Hat transformed my hair from patchy into shiny and healthy, and my sensitive scalp stopped breaking out into itchy sections. A smart bird feeder that will record video they can enjoy together after dinner, seeing what birds came to visit. WIRED reviewer Kat Merck says this is the best-looking smart bird feeder she's tested, and it's got a nice discount for Prime Day.

I have a problem. I'm obsessed with this slow cooker.
I already have a regular slow cooker and a multicooker at home, so I don't need this one. But I can't stop thinking about it. All I can think about is how fun it would be to have two things cooking side by side for holiday events, like two kinds of hot chocolate or mashed potatoes in one half with meatballs and gravy on the other. The pairings are endless, and I want it for every holiday party this season. Will I pull the trigger? I'll report back after Prime Day ends if I added it to my purchases.
Hatch Nightlights Have a Chokehold on My Nursery
I wrote this in our Smarter Buys newsletter last weekend, but my kiddo loves his Hatch Rest, which Hatch has now replaced with the Hatch Baby that's on sale for some small discounts (the deals are better off Amazon than on for this one). I find the noise and nightlight so comforting, I’m looking forward to testing the brand-new Hatch Sleep Clock, which seems to be for all ages. I also just found the Hatch Rest 2 in a non-Amazon refurbished deal, if you'd prefer the older model to the new.
Admit It. You Want the New Dyson.

The best Dyson experience is with the brand’s higher-end vacuums as well, and I was impressed that the Dyson V16 Piston Animal came with not only two different cleaner heads, but had an option to upgrade to Dyson’s newest Submarine mop head. It’s a powerhouse of a vacuum, and it’s on sale (both with and without the Submarine add on!) if it’s the one you’ve been dreaming of.
A Very Neutral Protein Powder
I’ve tried maybe six different protein powders, and this is the only one that doesn’t upset my stomach, so it’s been a repeat buy for over four years now. It’s a staple in any morning smoothie or emergency “oh no it’s 4 PM and I forgot to eat lunch” drink. It’s usually on sale, so this isn’t a huge discount, but hey, anything helps with kitchen staples. It comes in four flavors—I prefer the unflavored version, since I’m already adding plenty of sugar through fruits like bananas, mangos, and the like.
This Is the E-Reader Accessory I’d Buy a Fellow Reader
If you’re looking for easy birthday or Christmas gift ideas for a fellow reader who you know has some kind of e-reader device, I’ve got an easy gift for you. Strapsicle’s e-reader straps are on sale for Amazon Prime Day and can fit multiple e-reader devices. They're one of my favorite Kindle accessories, but I love that they're not limited to the Kindle ecosystem if you use a different e-reader. There’s one set for the six-inch base Kindles and Kobo Claras, and another for the seven-inch Kindle Paperwhite/Colorsoft and the Kobo Libra Colour. Both versions are on sale now, and come in a ton of fun colors that add a great pop to any e-reader (and are super comfortable!)
A Rug Good For Mother Earth (And Your Wallet)
I am literally obsessed with this rug. Every time people come over, they compliment it, and I have to blurt out, “It’s machine-washable, too!” I love this rug’s traditional pattern, inspired by Turkish folk art, that isn’t too busy. It’s woven from soft polyester chenille, which has an interesting, slightly fuzzy texture and resists stains and marks. I have it in the rust colorway, which adds a pop of color without being too flashy. It’s also OEKO-TEX and GRS (Global Recycled Standard) certified, so it’s kind to Mother Earth, too.
This Robot Vacuum Spotted So Many Stains on My Floor
If someone texted me right now asking which robot vacuum to buy during Prime Day, I know my answer. It’s the Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal.
I love this vacuum because it actually has the smarts it promises. I’ve tested more expensive vacuums that barely notice the dried spills on my floor or will just mark a single messy area, while the Shark’s UV light helps it find stains everywhere. It even found a spot on my floor I know I spilled orange juice on on months prior and I guess never properly cleaned. Thanks to the Shark, it’s clean now. It’s on sale for Prime Day and truly a great buy.
I’m Not Saying This E-Reader Will Save Your Marriage, But…
My dad group chat asked about the one thing they should buy for Prime Day 2026, and I had to go with the Kindle Paperwhite. If you like to read in bed, and maybe you have a spouse who’s trying to sleep, and maybe, hypothetically, your spouse gets mad when your light is still on, there’s really no better way to stay literate and partnered at the same time. And there’s no better time to buy a Kindle. Reading something actually good at night instead of doomscrolling: a fantastic little routine upgrade!
Digital Calendars Rule for Families. This One’s the Best Deal.
My favorite gadget this year has been a digital wall calendar, and that came as a big surprise to me. I tried one once before and hated it, and thought I’d feel that way about every version. Boy, was I wrong. These handy devices fit easily into my home to show me my family’s various calendars, our to-do lists, our meal plans, and even doubles as a digital photo frame (my favorite part!)
I’ve tried a lot of models since then, all of which I like better. Just about every single digital wall calendar I recommend is on sale, but the best deal for what you get is the Everblog HomeCal. It’s a smooth, simple interface that reminds me of Skylight, but you’ll get it for a little cheaper than Skylight right now and won’t have to worry about a paywall.
I Keep This Kinda Terrible Power Bank in My Car
This MagSafe power bank has a laughable 5,000-mAh capacity, which is paltry compared to the beefy batteries inside most of our phones. But while it won’t get you enough juice to scroll Instagram Reels while you avoid eye contact with cuties at the bar, it will get you enough to turn on your phone in a pinch if it dies while you’re out hiking in the wilderness. So I keep it around in case of emergencies, and the unobtrusive form factor doesn’t get in the way of bigger, more superior power banks inside my backpack or glovebox.
Prime Day Has Become My Maternity Stock-Up Session
I’m currently expecting my second child, and at almost six months pregnant, it’s time for me to face the music. That music is the fact that I can’t keep ignoring the large purchases I need to make…and that none of my pants fit anymore, just in time for it to get colder outside.
It makes Prime Day a pretty good opportunity for me and my growing shopping list. Right now, I’m checking out on the DaVinci Suzy Recliner Glider that the internet has promised me is a dupe for the popular Babyletto glider. I’ll be quick to judge if that’s accurate or not, but I’m thrilled to find it on sale and that it looks large enough for my preschooler to squeeze into it with me and baby if he wants to. I also stocked up on a few pairs of CRZ Yoga’s maternity leggings that have a $5 discount right now. It’s not a ton, but I’d rather save a little wherever I can, especially since I bought a couple of pairs.
It’s Never Too Late to Start Skincare
As I approach middle age, I realized it’s time to start taking better care of my skin. I finally boarded the K-Beauty train (thanks, Marshalls!) and found that eye patches do wonders for my face. The editors at our sister publication, Allure, recommend the Peptide Collagen Hydrogen Eye Patch from CosRx, a respected Korean skin care company. With vitamin B12 and hyaluronic acid to help soothe, smooth, and moisturize under the eyes, while peptides encourage collagen production and help tighten the skin. I’m looking forward to adding this to my nightly cleansing regimen, and with 33 percent off during Prime Day, it’s worth trying.
My Annual Wireless Earbuds Restock
Every year, I end up buying a new pair of wireless earbuds during Amazon Prime Day, and this year was no different. I somehow have three separate pairs of AirPods that only have the right earbud. And after hearing my colleagues rave about the low price of the latest Apple AirPods, I knew I’d have to keep the tradition alive. The noise-canceling and transparency abilities are touted as some of the best you can find in an earbud. I don’t really care about the extra features like a built-in heart rate sensor and live translation; I just wanted to have a left earbud again. And I’m betting that at the very least, these will.

Electric shock gloves deemed too painful by US Army are being rolled out by ICE
An October 2024 US Army trial found that role-playing soldiers stopped resisting within seconds of being shocked, with test subjects reporting lingering fear and soreness

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement is moving forward with plans to equip its officers with electric-shock gloves despite an internal military study showing the devices caused intense pain and fear during testing on Army personnel.
ICE signed a $16.7 million contract in August to purchase 6,000 pairs of the devices, known as the G.L.O.V.E., short for “Generated Low Output Voltage Emitter,” according to government records obtained by American Oversight and reported by the Associated Press.
The Department of Homeland Security previously indicated in a public notice that it planned to spend up to $20 million on the technology to acquire thousands of “conductive distraction and de-escalation devices” by March. The contract reportedly describes the equipment as “a low-impact tool” intended for situations where a person actively resists arrest or poses a clear threat, according to American Oversight, a nonpartisan government watchdog group.
Manufactured by Compliant Technologies LLC, based in Lexington, Kentucky, the equipment functions as standard patrol gear until an officer activates a switch. The device delivers an electrical charge upon direct contact with skin, targeting peripheral nerve endings to cause immediate pain rather than the full-body neuromuscular incapacitation typical of a Taser.
According to an October 2024 U.S. Army study conducted at the military prison at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas, test participants playing the role of combative inmates stopped resisting seconds after receiving shocks. The report noted that test subjects were left with “fatigue, soreness and excessive apprehensiveness to being shocked again.”
The 38-page report — conducted by the Naval Surface Warfare Center Indian Head Demonstration and Assessment Team — noted that the trial did not produce statistically relevant data to make predictions on efficacy, nor did it evaluate the device’s broader health or safety effects on humans.
The study concluded that “after experiencing the effects of the GLOVE … participants stated just seeing the GLOVE was enough to make them want to comply.”
Researchers observed that although the device did not significantly alter transport times during inmate escorts, it “increased the efficiency” of forced cell extractions and disturbance responses, and it reduced physical exertion for guards.
“GLOVE provides a boost in confidence to smaller or less trained members,” the Army study reported, adding that “inmate compliance was immediate.”
However, tests also showed that wet or oily skin intensified the shock, with one participant reporting discomfort lasting 30 minutes.
ICE leaders had access to the study before finalizing the purchase contract. The agency has defended the acquisition, framing the gloves as de-escalation tools that offer a safer alternative to lethal force when handling civil disturbances or subduing subjects during arrests and deportations.
But civil rights groups and lawmakers have raised concerns over potential misuse as the devices are integrated into federal immigration enforcement.
The procurement comes amid a broader expansion of authority for ICE’s Homeland Security Investigations division. Internal government documents obtained by legal advocacy group Democracy Forward and shared with The Independent reveal that HSI has also been tasked with probing voter registration groups and targeting noncitizen voter allegations ahead of the midterms, using data supplied by right-wing activists and federal voter roll databases.
Advocates warn that giving expanding enforcement powers to the agency increases the potential for harm. Records obtained earlier this year by American Oversight revealed a nearly 400 percent spike in ICE use-of-force incidents during the first months of the second Trump administration, alongside record-high deaths in custody. According to American Oversight, ICE officers have shot and killed at least five people since last year, including two U.S. citizens.
“The military assessment in ICE’s own files shows that these gloves can cause ‘intense pain’ and force compliance. It does not establish that they are safe,” Chioma Chukwu, executive director of American Oversight, said. “Everyone should be alarmed that ICE is preparing to deploy a tool designed to inflict, at best, intense pain, without showing that it is safe for the people who will be subjected to it.”
Jenn Rolnick Borchetta, deputy project director on policing at the American Civil Liberties Union, said in August that the discreet nature of the device increased the risk of abuse.
“ICE spent the last year showing this country they are too quick to use force. Now they will be able to deploy electric shocks with the slight push of a button that maybe nobody else can see them do,” Borchetta said. “Introducing gloves that can so easily be used to deliver terrible pain in encounters is a recipe for harm to the public.”
Sen. Catherine Cortez Masto of Nevada noted that ICE has failed to respond to an August 27 inquiry sent by 16 Democratic senators demanding details on deployment policies and safety protocols.
“Without ICE’s responses to legitimate questions from 16 United States senators, the American public is being left in the dark about how these electric-shock gloves are being deployed and what, if any, training the agents who use them have received,” Cortez Masto said.
Proponents of the technology maintain that the devices reduce injuries during physical confrontations. John Peters, president of the Institute for the Prevention of In-Custody Deaths, said that the stimulus was designed to create a quick distraction.
“It’s immediate and sharp, and it will distract you,” Peters said. “I call it like a bee sting. For smaller officers or weaker officers or older officers, I think it has a great advantage.”
Compliant Technologies guidelines state the gloves require biannual recertification and prohibit use against high-risk populations, including pregnant women, children, the elderly or individuals displaying only verbal defiance.
The manufacturer has also faced legal challenges over the device’s use. A pending lawsuit in Kentucky alleges a 43-year-old man died in a county jail after officers shocked him 40 times using a combination of a Taser and the shock gloves.
White House border czar Tom Homan indicated that operational deployment may take time as ICE finishes training modules and administrative policies.
In a statement to the Associated Press, ICE stated that “officers are highly trained in de-escalation tactics,” though the agency did not directly address the findings of the military study.
The Independent has contacted ICE for further comment.

The story so far: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, announced on Monday (October 5, 2026) went jointly to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegeman and Georg Nagel “for their discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics.” The prize amount of 12 million Swedish kronor, to be shared equally between the Laureates.
How the brain functions and pulls the strings to guide feelings, behaviour and bodily functions has long been a mystery. It was in the 20th century, that researchers began to map areas of the brain to related functions, but the methods they used could not prove causal relationships. So, the image they developed of the brain was like a sketch map, full of question marks and unknowns, as the Nobel committee described it. Now all this is changing, thanks to revolutionary techniques including optogenetics.

India’s supreme court has demanded accountability from the government and the senior election body over a controversial exercise that has led to the deletion of tens of millions of voters from the electoral roll and prompted mass protests.
Demonstrations have erupted across the country in recent days as opposition parties, student groups and the youth-led Cockroach movement have demanded the resignation of Gyanesh Kumar, the head of the Election Commission of India (ECI).
They have accused Kumar of overseeing a direct attack on India’s democracy through an exercise to verify and “purify” the electoral roll in states across the country, which so far has led to 130 million names being removed. In Delhi, hundreds of people were detained as they tried to protest over the weekend.
On Monday, the supreme court issued notices to Narendra Modi’s government, the ECI and Kumar to demand answers over concerns raised about the voter list revision, saying they expected all “to respond in a clear, transparent manner”.
The ECI has claimed the exercise is simply cleaning electoral rolls of duplicate, dead and ineligible names, as well as removing “illegal infiltrators”. However, large numbers of people in Delhi and states such as Bihar and West Bengal say they have been wrongly stripped of their vote and have struggled to get it back.
There are accusations that revision of the electoral rolls particularly targets minorities such as Muslims, who are traditionally not voters of Modi’s ruling Bharatiya Janata party (BJP).
The opposition alliance, led by the Congress party, have accused the ECI of being hand in glove with the government over alleged vote “chori” or cheating. Kumar was chosen to head the ECI by a panel headed by Modi.
While the exercise, known as the special intensive revision (SIR), began last year, widespread outrage only recently erupted after a report in the Indian Express newspaper revealed multiple irregularities in the process, which were flagged in more than a dozen internal objections.
The two petitions taken up by the supreme court on Monday alleged that the credibility of the ECI was now in question and called for an independent inquiry into the decisions taken by Kumar in how the SIR process was conducted.
“Deletions of voters have been made in the largest democracy,” said Menaka Guruswamy, a lawyer acting for one of the petitioners. “We have grown up with free and fair elections, that is not the case now.”
Another advocate told the supreme court judges that if action was not taken to ensure that India’s electoral rolls remained fair, “this country will burn”. Another hearing in the cases will be held next week.
The controversies over the ECI have once again driven India’s young people on to the streets in protest, amid rising frustration at the Modi government.
The Cockroach Janata party (CJP), which led massive unrest over the summer that forced the resignation of Modi’s education minister, have once again mobilised and called for the resignation of Kumar. Thousands of CJP supporters took to the streets of Mumbai last Friday in protest and another demonstration was held on Saturday in Delhi.
In Delhi, police have been criticised for their heavy-handed approach to stopping any student groups protesting in the heart of the capital. Officers have been accused of sexually assaulting three journalists at the protests over the weekend and hundreds of young people were forced on to police buses. Delhi police said it was investigating the assault claims.

Man City charges: Erling Haaland encourages club's fans to stay positive after guilty verdict
Man City were found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission; City have lodged their appeal against the verdict
Thursday 8 October 2026 16:04, UK
"Stick together, enjoy the ride and smile," is Erling Haaland's message to Man City fans.
The club have launched an appeal against the verdict of an independent commission finding them guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules.
City insist in their statement they are "innocent" and have described the judgement against them as "opinion" and claimed it "contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe".
The independent commission found that between 2009/10 and 2017/18, Man City arranged "sham" contracts with a number of its commercial partners as part of a "disguised funding scheme" to artificially inflate the club's revenues by £830m.
Amid all the off-field news, Haaland and his team-mates go to Anfield on Sunday, live on Sky Sports, to face Liverpool.
Asked what he would say to the City supporters ahead of that game, Haaland said: "They're going to have a good time.
"We have to stick together. We have to stay with each other, and we have to stay positive. No matter what happens in life, we always have to have a smile.
"So we have to stay positive, look ahead, and try to win football games and try to enjoy the situation and win the game.
"We have to stick together; we have to spread the love to each other. So yeah: stick together, and enjoy the ride and smile."

Haaland - the son of former City player Alf-Inge Haaland - says he considers himself a fan of City, too, and referenced his connection with Manchester.
"I care a lot about the city, I have to say. I care a lot about the fans because I'm a fan myself, and I feel with them as well."
City's matches with Liverpool became big rivalry games during the Pep Guardiola and Jurgen Klopp eras at the two clubs and Haaland is looking forward to the occasion.
"It's always special to play against Liverpool. Especially with Pep and Klopp. I remember sitting in Salzburg and Dortmund and watching the games, how much they pushed each other. It's always special games there.
"I won there, I drew there, I lost. So it's always special, and every Premier League game is different, and every game against Liverpool is always special."
What did the independent commission find?
- Manchester City arranged "sham" contracts with a number of its commercial partners as part of a "disguised funding scheme" to artificially inflate the club's revenues by £830m.
- The club filed accounts that concealed the true state of its finances.
- Manchester City were significantly in breach of both the Premier League's and UEFA's spending limits and broke "well over 100" Premier League regulations.
- Manchester City failed to co-operate and act in good faith towards the league during the investigation, with three out of four alleged breaches upheld and one charge not proven.
- The commission also said it was "regrettable" that a decision had taken so long to reach, with the hearing having taken place between September and December 2024.
City: Process was not impartial
Following the publication of the guilty verdict on September 29, a Manchester City statement read: "Manchester City FC is both disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League commission, that has been published today.
"The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case. The club will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums.
"The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements uncompleted. Manchester City FC will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it, on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe.
"The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.
"The club is obviously restricted in what it can say further until all future proceedings are complete."
Manchester City's statement erroneously refers to a Premier League commission. It is an independent commission.
Why Man City's appeal could drag into 2027
Latest from Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol and Amar Mehta:
Manchester City's appeal could drag on into next year if they argue that the process should not be run according to Premier League rules which were introduced for this season.
City have filed their appeal and the new rules about appeals state that this part of the disciplinary process has to be concluded within 12 weeks and the appeal hearing can last no longer than five days.
City's lawyers could argue that they were charged in 2023 and a hearing was held in 2024 - when the rules about a speeded-up appeals process were not in the Premier League Handbook.
A legal expert told Sky Sports News Manchester City would have a strong case for arguing that the new rules should not apply in this case.
The new rules were introduced to ensure that clubs, where possible, were punished in the same season as relevant rule breaches.

Some Medicare patients owe more in coinsurance than the hospital paid for their drug. That arithmetic sounds impossible. It is a consequence of the 340B drug discount program and Medicare’s payment formula. Now the Department of Health and Human Services, where I work, is proposing to narrow that gap.
Congress created the 340B drug discount program in 1992 to financially support safety net hospitals that serve low-income patients. Drug manufacturers must give them steep discounts. But Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial insurers generally reimburse them at the full amount, allowing these hospitals to keep the spread above the discounted purchasing costs.
A new report from the Department of Health and Human Services shows other unintended consequences of this well-intended program. The spread grows with the price of the drug. It therefore rewards hospitals for using more and costlier drugs and makes physician practices and infusion clinics more valuable after a 340B hospital acquires them. The patient’s treatment needn’t change. The owner and billing site do.
The 340B program has exploded: Eligible drug purchases rose from $12 billion in 2015 to $81 billion in 2024, mostly at hospitals, as shown in the report. Those purchases are now larger than net Medicare Part B and Medicaid drug spending overall and, among public prescription drug programs, are smaller only than Medicare Part D.
A 340B hospital that buys another hospital or a physician practice can register more off-campus clinics and contract pharmacies and capture more spread. Hospital off-campus clinic sites grew from about 7,000 in 2013 to more than 34,000 in 2023, often in neighborhoods that are wealthier and better-insured than that of the parent hospital. Contract pharmacies grew from roughly 1,300 in 2010 to more than 31,000 by mid-2026, dominated by the largest chains.
With greater bargaining power after acquisitions, hospital systems can negotiate higher commercial prices for health care services, which can in turn raise premiums. Newly acquired hospital outpatient sites can also add facility fees to non-drug services. The effects of 340B show up as larger, more expensive hospital systems and a bigger bill for patients, employers, and taxpayers. The program’s ripple effects contribute to the broader problems facing the U.S. health care system.
Medicare payment for Part B drugs is typically based on average sales price (ASP). Beginning in 2018, the first Trump administration narrowed the spread in Medicare by paying hospitals for 340B drugs’ ASP minus 22.5% rather than the usual statutory standard of ASP plus 6%, based on an earlier estimate of their average minimum discount.
Overall outpatient drug payments rose nearly 15% a year from 2015 through 2017. Once the lower rate was fully in effect, inflation-adjusted payments largely plateaued. Payments for the affected 340B drugs held near $7 billion from 2019 through 2021. It is clear that Medicare payment policy influences outpatient drug spending.
The Supreme Court ruled in 2022 that HHS couldn’t vary payment rates by hospital group without first conducting the acquisition-cost survey required by statute. The court didn’t find that hospitals were economically entitled to the markup. It found that HHS lacked a procedural prerequisite. After the lower rate ended and ASP plus 6% returned for these drugs, annual payments for the affected drugs rose from $7.1 billion in 2021 to $10.7 billion in 2023 — a $3.6 billion increase. Overall outpatient drug payments rose from $14.3 billion in 2021 to $17.6 billion in 2023.
Restoring the higher rate meant paying hospitals more for the same drugs. The $3.6 billion increase combines that direct payment effect with induced changes in hospitals’ dispensing quantities and drug manufacturers’ underlying prices. The larger spread also strengthens hospitals’ incentive to choose costlier drugs and move treatment into 340B billing sites.
Off-campus hospital departments benefited too. From 2021 to 2023, payments for their affected 340B drugs rose about $800 million even as claims fell and the number of beneficiaries remained similar. Although these amounts do not tell us how many practices hospitals acquired because of the markup, they indicate the additional financial incentives for acquisitions.
On April 18, 2025, President Trump directed HHS to obtain the cost information the statute requires. CMS surveyed hospitals from January through April 2026 and has proposed paying for affected 340B drugs at ASP minus 33.4% in 2027. CMS estimates that Medicare drug payments would fall by $4.55 billion in the first year and beneficiary drug copayments by $1.15 billion.
For a drug with an ASP of $1,000, a beneficiary’s standard 20% coinsurance would fall from $212 to $133.20. The prescription hasn’t changed. The patient’s share of the hospital’s bill has. Narrowing the spread also weakens the incentive to steer patients toward costlier drugs and to acquire physician practices and infusion clinics — the very behaviors that have made care more expensive.
There’s an important lesson here. A small, well-intended discount for safety net hospitals became a large institutional subsidy with expensive unintended consequences. Under the proposed rule, hospitals would still receive their 340B drug discounts. What would change is Medicare’s payment for those drugs at affected hospitals. Congress provided for a survey of hospitals’ acquisition costs, and CMS says its proposed rate would “more accurately align Medicare payments with hospital drug acquisition costs.”
Medicare patients should not pay coinsurance as though the discount did not exist.
Casey B. Mulligan is the chief economist and chief regulatory officer at HHS.

Journalist to be crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute
- Published
Prince Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma Nyabongo I, who is set to be crowned king of Uganda's Tooro kingdom later, has long been a familiar face in the country.
For many Ugandans, he was known not as the heir to the throne, but as a storyteller, as a long-serving anchor and editor at the state broadcaster.
But Kijanangoma, 56, has now become the subject of media attention himself - his rise to the Tooro throne sparking controversy and widespread reactions beyond the country.
Tooro is one of Uganda's four main officially recognised historical kingdoms. For the last 31 years, it has been headed by King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, who was once known as a "boy king", after ascending to the throne as an infant.
Oyo became king in 1995 at the age of just three, following the death of his father. Then the world's youngest monarch, he ruled until he died last month from cancer, aged just 34.
The coronation is a day for celebration, involving traditional practices starting from midnight. The new king then walks about 4km (2.5 miles) to the official Karuziika royal palace where he is crowned.
A mock fight follows, to signify that kingship does not come easy, and he is then blessed by members of the royal Babiito clan, the Tooro kingdom's Information Minister Charles Mwanguhya told the BBC Focus on Africa podcast.
He performs other ceremonies that signifies his assumption of the throne, before he sits on the throne and an actual crown placed on his head to signify his new authority, his new position as the new Tooro king.
But the selection of Kijanangoma as king was far from straightforward.
According to tradition, a recognised son of the late king should succeed him. Close members of the royal family said Oyo had left a young son and a will with instructions that the child should be next on the throne.
But the son has never been revealed to the public and nor was he recognised by the committee of 21 Babiito clan members who choose the king and eventually selected Kijanangoma.
The late King Oyo was never publicly married, and little is known about his wife or their son.
Nonetheless his mother, Queen Best Kemigisa, argued that the late king's will ought to have been respected.
However, the royal succession committee ignored her wishes, insisting their selection process was conducted in accordance with Tooro customs and traditions.
The new king has thus found himself at the centre of a succession dispute, with Kemigisa and her close relatives unhappy with the outcome.
Kemigisa referred to Kijanangoma's selection as the "announcement of a second king" being "made after the will of King Oyo was read to members of the royal family".
"As a mother, that was extraordinarily painful," she said, describing celebrations for the next king taking place "only metres from where my son's body lay".
The queen later said Oyo's son, who was in the US state of Texas, had been due to return home but that could not happen amid a "tense and polarised succession dispute".
"No child should be placed in circumstances where returning to his father's homeland could mean being drawn into hostility and conflict," Kemigisa asserted in a post on X.
But according to the Tooro kingdom's information minister, the son being talked about "hasn't been presented anywhere, which means there is a growing acceptance that sad as it may be, King Oyo didn't leave a son behind".
While King Oyo inherited the crown from his father, Mwanguhya told the BBC "the crown has moved to a different line within the ruling clan".
A king must come from the Babiito clan, specifically the lineage of King George David Matthew Kamurasi Rukidi III, according to royal palace sources.
Kijanangoma and the late King Oyo are cousins. Both are grandsons of Rukidi III, the 11th king, or Omukama, who ruled the Tooro kingdom from 1928 to 1965.
Kijanangoma was among several people who were considered for the role, including Prince George Desmond Kamurasi, who plays football for one of the UK's best-known amateur clubs.
According to the succession committee, the South East Dons captain and goalkeeper declined the offer of the throne, citing other responsibilities.
After he was formally announced, Kijanangoma promised that the palace would be open to the people, while vowing to focus on unity and development.
"I ask you for one thing - they have given me this title as king but I cannot work alone, I have to work with you," he said.
Uganda's traditional kings have no formal political authority, but they retain cultural influence and command significant loyalty in the communities they lead.
The country is home to four main kingdoms, the largest and most prominent being Buganda in the central region, which encompasses the capital Kampala.
The kingdoms were abolished in 1967, but the government under President Yoweri Museveni restored them in the early 1990s.
The government said this was to promote cultural pride and national unity, but the move has also been interpreted as a way of appeasing communities and fostering political loyalty.
Amid the succession dispute, the government backed the Babiito clan's choice of Kijanangoma. Attorney General Sam Mayanja said the Tooro kingdom was cleared to go ahead with the coronation, as there had not been a formal complaint against him.
The date of the coronation was announced by the government and Museveni is scheduled to attend.
The president's son and the head of the military, Muhoozi Kainerugaba, has also publicly supported Kijanangoma. "Long may he reign," he posted on X.
Kijanangoma's very name points to his royal heritage.
His father, the first Kijanangoma, was born in the year King Rukidi III became king. The king gave him the name, which means the "one who comes with the royal drum".
The drum of royalty, foretold two generations earlier, is now returning to its bearer.
Kijanangoma was born in 1970 and raised at their family home at Kidukuru village in Fort Portal, about 300 km (186 miles) from Kampala.
He left the village to pursue further studies and graduated with a mass communication degree from Uganda's prestigious Makerere University in 1999.
He worked as a broadcaster in a career spanning more than two decades, including in neighbouring Rwanda and at home, with the Uganda Broadcasting Corporation.
The years spent engaging with the public, the interactions with leaders and the exposure to national affairs in his work as a journalist may yet serve him well as he returns to the community he came from, this time as their leader.
After he was named king, Kijanangoma said he would use the connections he had built up over 21 years working as a journalist "to get good things for our people".
His mother, Assimwe Yusta Kijanangoma, is confident that he is well prepared for his new role. She says his upbringing was deeply rooted in tradition.
"I really raised him with the teachings of the old kingdom of a cane and instructions and scolding. I laugh with him, and other times I scold him," she told the BBC.
She added: "Eddy is well-mannered, he does not fight, or shout, even when wronged, he says a few words and does not go so much into it."
She feels good for her son, although she admits to having mixed emotions, especially as her son is taking over after the death of a "great man".
